meta.title: oscp lab-setup — Kali on VMware Fusion for OSCP/OSWE/HTB/CTF
meta.note: Build a clean Kali attacker box end to end: install, guest tools, update, toolset, snapshot, VPN, MTU — plus the gotchas and fixes. oscp lab-setup <section> to zoom in.
meta.flow: vm -> install -> guest-tools -> update -> tools -> snapshot -> vpn -> mtu (tune)

sections.name: 1. Create the VM (Apple Silicon)
sections.goal: Pick the right ISO and give the VM enough resources up front.
steps: Use the Kali ARM64 installer ISO — on Apple Silicon, never the x86-64 ISO
Install from disc or image -> select the ARM64 .iso
No Kali profile? pick 'Linux ARM 64-bit' (e.g. Debian 13 ARM) — a VM compatibility profile, not 'Kali = Debian'
CPU/RAM: 4 cores, 4-8 GB RAM (8 GB if the host can spare it; leave memory for macOS)
Disk: 40 GB minimum, 60 GB+ better — undersized disks cause partitioning failures
Network: 'Share with my Mac' (NAT) — Kali uses the Mac's internet, it is not on the LAN
3D accel: leave default/off; enable only if stable
sections.why: NAT is the sensible OSCP default; Bridged exposes Kali on the LAN and Host-only has no internet by itself. Getting disk/RAM right up front avoids a reinstall.
sections.gotcha: Wrong-arch ISO won't boot; <40 GB disk -> partitioning errors; Bridged/Host-only -> no internet. The lab's published network requirement overrides NAT.

sections.name: 2. Install Kali
sections.goal: Complete the guided install and boot clean.
steps: Boot the installer, complete the guided install
Partitioning fails? fix the disk size first — don't continue on an undersized disk
Eject/disconnect the installer ISO, then boot the virtual disk — or it 'reinstalls' every boot
sections.why: Leaving the ISO attached is the classic 'it keeps booting the installer' trap.

sections.name: 3. VMware guest integration (shared folder + clipboard)
sections.goal: Shared folders, clipboard and drag-and-drop between macOS and Kali.
steps: sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y open-vm-tools open-vm-tools-desktop fuse && sudo reboot
Settings -> Sharing: enable Shared Folders, add the host folder (R/W) — e.g. share name kali-shared
vmware-hgfsclient ; sudo mkdir -p /mnt/hgfs ; sudo vmhgfs-fuse .host:/ /mnt/hgfs -o allow_other
Clipboard broken? Isolation: enable Copy/Paste + Drag/Drop, then reinstall + reboot
sudo apt install --reinstall -y open-vm-tools open-vm-tools-desktop fuse && sudo reboot
sections.why: Shared folders and clipboard are separate VMware features — one can work while the other is broken; the -desktop package + a reboot restores clipboard.
sections.gotcha: vmware-hgfsclient lists the share but /mnt/hgfs is empty -> the mount point didn't exist / wasn't mounted. A manual mount may need repeating after reboot (make it persistent or re-run vmhgfs-fuse).

sections.name: 4. Update & upgrade
sections.goal: Current packages and a valid keyring.
steps: sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y kali-archive-keyring && sudo apt update
Disk full mid-upgrade? (if truly full, you undersized the disk)
sections.why: full-upgrade (not plain upgrade) handles Kali's rolling dependency changes; a stale keyring is the usual NO_PUBKEY cause.

sections.name: 5. Install the toolset
steps: sudo apt install -y seclists feroxbuster bloodhound netexec ffuf gobuster nmap
Python tools via pipx (avoids pip PEP-668 errors)
sudo apt install -y pipx && pipx ensurepath
pipx install impacket ; pipx install certipy-ad ; pipx install git+https://github.com/dirkjanm/BloodHound.py
Pivoting binaries — download chisel + ligolo-ng for Kali AND the target's arch (both ends)
Keep winPEAS/linpeas/pspy/mimikatz/Rubeus in ~/tools to serve to targets over HTTP/SMB
sections.why: kali-linux-default covers most of it; pipx keeps Python tools isolated and sidesteps the newer 'externally-managed-environment' pip error. Per-tool usage: oscp atlas <tool>.
sections.gotcha: System-wide `pip install` now errors (PEP 668) -> use pipx or a venv. rockyou ships gzipped -> gunzip it once.

sections.name: 6. Take a baseline snapshot
sections.goal: A fast rollback point once everything works.
steps: Fusion -> Snapshots -> Take Snapshot — name it e.g. Kali-clean-tools-working
Snapshot again before risky installs; restore via Snapshot Manager
sections.why: A snapshot is a quick rollback — NOT a backup of your files. Keep loot/notes in the shared folder or off-VM.

sections.name: 7. Connect to the lab VPN (OffSec / HTB / other)
sections.goal: Connect with OpenVPN and verify the tunnel.
steps: Connect WITH sudo — root is required to create tun0, set its IP and add routes
Wait for the lines: 'TUN/TAP device tun0 opened' then 'Initialization Sequence Completed'
HTB / PG / THM: same, with that platform's pack (keep the terminal open)
Verify in a second terminal (expect an inet on tun0)
ip addr show tun0 ; ip route
AUTH_FAILED or 'Duplicate VPN session Detected'? kill stale clients, wait, reconnect
sudo pkill openvpn ; sleep 5 ; sudo openvpn --config ~/Desktop/universal.ovpn
Disconnect with Ctrl-C in the OpenVPN terminal
sections.why: MUST run with sudo: without root, OpenVPN cannot open tun0, so there's no tunnel (ifconfig shows no tun0). `sudo openvpn file.ovpn` and `sudo openvpn --config file.ovpn` are identical — a bare filename IS treated as --config; the thing that matters is the sudo, not --config. (No need to chmod +x the .ovpn — it's a config, not a script.) Keep the terminal open while connected; tun0 getting an inet = tunnel up. Use only YOUR profile and keep it private. Connect to ONE lab VPN at a time (route overlap breaks traffic).
sections.gotcha: 'Duplicate VPN session Detected' / AUTH_FAILED usually means a previous OpenVPN client is still holding a session: `sudo pkill openvpn`, wait ~5 min for OffSec's cooldown, then reconnect with ONLY your current .ovpn. No tun0 at all after 'Peer Connection Initiated' = you forgot sudo. 'Initialization Sequence Completed' means connected, not that routing/DNS work (see the mtu section). Two VPNs / overlapping subnets -> traffic breaks.

sections.name: 8. VPN up but traffic stalls -> diagnose MTU
sections.goal: Find and work around packet-size (MTU) problems.
steps: Temporary fix — record the original MTU first
sudo ip link set dev tun0 mtu 1300 ; ip link show tun0
Same temporary fix with ifconfig — record the original MTU first
sudo ifconfig tun0 mtu 1250 ; ifconfig tun0
sections.why: A connected VPN doesn't prove all packet sizes/routes/DNS work. Lowering MTU avoids fragmentation / path-MTU black-holes on some paths. 1300 (ip link) and 1250 (ifconfig) are TEST values, not universal — restore the original MTU and check routes/DNS/firewall/profile if it doesn't help. ICMP may be blocked, so a failed ping alone isn't proof.

sections.name: 9. Best setup per exam / platform
sections.goal: One clean base; add context-specific tooling per engagement.

rows: NAT, 8 GB RAM; kali-linux-default + impacket/nxc/bloodhound/chisel/seclists; snapshot before the exam
Burp, source-review tooling, your IDE, more RAM; web/debug focus
that platform's VPN pack; ligolo-ng/chisel; broad tooling (kali-everything optional)

sections.why: Keep the base lean and snapshotted, then branch per engagement — don't rebuild for each.

sections.name: 10. Gotchas -> quick fix
sections.goal: The common failures and their one-line remediation.

rows: wrong ISO arch -> use the Kali ARM64 ISO
disk < 40 GB -> make it bigger and reinstall
Bridged/Host-only -> switch to NAT (Share with my Mac)
Isolation: enable it + reinstall open-vm-tools-desktop + reboot
sudo pkill openvpn ; wait ~5 min ; reconnect with your .ovpn only
VPN: no tun0 after 'Peer Connection Initiated'
you forgot sudo -> run openvpn with sudo (root needed for tun0)
needs a USB adapter via the USB menu, NOT the NAT/Bridged NIC

sections.why: Most lab-setup pain is one of these; fix the cause, then re-snapshot.

sections.name: 11. Verify everything
sections.goal: Confirm shares, guest tools and networking.
sections.why: A 60-second health check after setup (and after each reboot) catches a dropped mount or guest-tools service before it wastes your time.

sections.name: 12. Lab variables ($ip / $domain / $user) across tabs
sections.goal: Persist the current target's IP/domain/creds as shell variables, auto-synced across terminal tabs, with /etc/hosts kept in step.
steps: Read the shipped helper first — never source shell code you haven't looked at
Load it from ~/.zshrc (add ONE line yourself), then open a new tab
Set creds — AUTHORISED lab creds only; they are stored in plaintext
sections.why: Variables persist because each setter WRITES them to ~/.labenv (not just exports them); ~/.zshrc sources that file on every new shell, and a precmd hook re-sources it when another tab changed it — so set the IP once and $ip works in every tab. Using $ip/$user/$password in commands beats retyping them and cuts copy-paste mistakes.
sections.gotcha: Plaintext creds in ~/.labenv -> chmod 600 and use lab-only passwords, never real/reused ones (the shipped labinfo masks them on screen). Changing the domain can leave a STALE /etc/hosts line — the shipped script removes the old mapping, but review `tail /etc/hosts` when switching labs. Do NOT add '%sudo ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' just to avoid the sudo prompt on the /etc/hosts write — that's far too broad; keep normal sudo and type your password.
